openMenu Virtual Folder Bundle, based on Derek Pascarella's 1.7.2, with this fork's openMenu and Card Manager.

## openMenu
- **Controller editor and Joy-Con motion page.** In the File screen, select a controller and press A to open its settings. This works with iBlue and Pico2Maple adapters. The DC API only ever talks to the controller unit, never a memory card.
- **File screen safety.** No copy or delete can reach the wrong card: the card is checked against its listing, and nothing is written while the card is being read. Format, colour and "use full size" check the card first. Serial VMU backups are written to a new file before the old one is replaced.
- **Smoother menus** (measured frame by frame in flycast: no dropped frames in the main menu, game list, information screen or Internet screen):
  - The game list draws a lightweight case on its card; the full case, with spine and back, appears in the information screen (Y), which is prepared while the list rests on a game.
  - The case and disc pictures are made much faster, and at start-up.
  - The main menu no longer hitches every 20 frames or so.
  - The Internet screen opens without its long pause. The network adapter is checked during start-up.
- Fixes: Settings rows could go blank after the game list had been opened; an on-screen keyboard bounds bug.

## Card Manager
- **Back** and **Spine** columns beside Artwork. Each shows whether the game has a back cover (BACK.DAT) or spine label (SPINE.DAT); click to open the artwork window on that picture.
- Builds for Windows, Linux and macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel). Each one carries this release's openMenu.

## Downloads
| File | For |
|---|---|
| `GDMENUCardManager.v1.7.2-ateam4-win-x64.zip` | Windows 10/11 64-bit (needs the .NET 6 Desktop Runtime) |
| `GDMENUCardManager.v1.7.2-ateam4-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux x64 (self-contained) |
| `GDMENUCardManager.v1.7.2-ateam4-osx-arm64-AppBundle.tar.gz` | macOS, Apple Silicon |
| `GDMENUCardManager.v1.7.2-ateam4-osx-x64-AppBundle.tar.gz` | macOS, Intel |
| `1ST_READ.BIN` | openMenu on its own (the Card Manager already includes it) |

The macOS bundles are ad-hoc signed. If macOS refuses to open the app, right-click it and choose Open, or run `xattr -cr GDMENUCardManager.app`.

Frame rates come from the flycast emulator. Please report anything that stutters or misbehaves on a real console.
